thread.title: Apple Price Target Hiked On App Store Growth As Bulls, Bears Battle

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: Apple Price Target Hiked On App Store Growth As Bulls, Bears Battle
text:
The App Store will be Apple 's ( AAPL ) largest and most significant contributor to services growth, brokerage Morgan Stanley said Thursday as it raised its price target on the iPhone maker.
X Katy Huberty, a Morgan Stanley analyst, raised her price target to 214 from 200.
"We counter the bears, arguing that App Store growth is sustainable," Huberty said in a note to clients. "We believe Services will pick up the growth baton and account for 67% of Apple revenue growth over the next five years."
Shares edged down a fraction to 188.15 The stock rallied after the company reported fiscal second-quarter earnings in April. The stock is up more than 10% thus far in 2018 and has jumped 24% from a year ago.
 Business Growth Misguided? An Instinet analyst earlier this week said Apple's recent rally based on rosy forecasts for services business growth is misguided. The company's services businesses include Apple Music, Apple Pay, AppleCare, iCloud, App Store and other offerings.
But Huberty contends the App Store has the potential to post double-digit growth over the next few years.
"We estimate that in the last 12 months, users have spent over $40 billion in the App Store, of which Apple collects roughly a 30% cut, implying the App Store generated slightly more than $12 billion of net revenue for Apple in the last 12 months, up 29% year-over-year," Huberty went on to say. "With diversifying growth drivers, we believe the App Store has significant growth runway ahead and we forecast it growing at a 26% revenue CAGR (compound annual growth rate) through 2021."
